root_cause.text: The function `usbip_pack_ret_submit()` unconditionally overwrites `urb->number_of_packets` from the network response PDU without validating that the value does not exceed the original allocation size, allowing a malicious USB/IP server to send a larger value that causes a heap out-of-bounds write when `usbip_recv_iso()` iterates over `urb->iso_frame_desc[]`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch description states: "When a USB/IP client receives a RET_SUBMIT response, usbip_pack_ret_submit() unconditionally overwrites urb->number_of_packets from the network PDU. This value is subsequently used as the loop bound in usbip_recv_iso() and usbip_pad_iso() to iterate over urb->iso_frame_desc[], a flexible array whose size was fixed at URB allocation time based on the *original* number_of_packets from the CMD_SUBMIT. A malicious USB/IP server can set number_of_packets in the response to a value larger than what was originally submitted, causing a heap out-of-bounds write." The patch adds a check (`if (rpdu->number_of_packets < 0 || rpdu->number_of_packets > urb->number_of_packets)`) before the overwrite to clamp the value to zero on violation.

intent_record.how: This prevents a supplied packet count from being out of range, which could cause an out-of-bounds write when accessing the iso_frame_desc flexible array in usbip_recv_iso() and usbip_pad_iso(). Setting the count to 0 ensures those functions safely return early.
